item.title: Seahawks star Uchenna Nwosu fined for horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks played their most complete game of the season last Sunday, routing the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 behind efficient offense and a masterful defensive performance. They did not, however, come away unscathed in the NFL’s fine book. Unsurprisingly, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was docked some money after he was penalized for a horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes. Nwosu was held on the same play, so there were offsetting penalties called and a replayed down. On the next snap, Derick Hall had a crunching strip-sack on the Chiefs quarterback, but neither Nwosu nor Jarran Reed could recover the loose ball, and Mahomes somehow recovered his own fumble to preserve Kansas City’s eventual field goal. Rumor has it that Mike Tirico is still saying, “STILL OUT!” to this day. Seahawks edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was fined $17,911 for his horse-collar tackle of Patrick Mahomes. It was the only fine on either team. pic.twitter.com/fWWiJaTxVg — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 31, 2026 Horse-collar tackles are among the offenses that the NFL has deemed suspension worthy for repeat offenders. If Nwosu commits two more horse-collar penalties this year, he will serve an automatic one-game ban. No other Seahawks were fined. The immediate greater worry for Nwosu is his availability for Monday night against the Chicago Bears, as he’s listed as doubtful for the game.

item.title: Pierre Sage on the brink as Jean-Philippe Mateta's early red card hands Tottenham a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Crystal Palace FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Pierre Sage's future at Crystal Palace is hanging by a thread after Jean-Philippe Mateta's 13th-minute red card paved the way for a 2-0 defeat at Tottenham. Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke both headed home as Roberto De Zerbi's side won three games in a row for the first time in 616 days, while Palace slipped into the Premier League's bottom three. Mateta red card leaves Palace with 10 men Palace made an encouraging start, with Mateta firing straight at Antonin Kinsky, but disaster struck in the 13th minute. As Micky van de Ven passed the ball back to his goalkeeper, Mateta's studs caught the Tottenham defender on the back of the heel. According to the Guardian, referee Michael Oliver initially showed a yellow card, but the outcome was inevitable once VAR sent him to the monitor. Not for the first time this season, after Axel Disasi's red card against Ipswich last month, Palace were down to 10 men with most of the game still to play. Gray and Van Hecke head Tottenham to a third straight win Palace kept Tottenham at bay for a while, but they played a part in their own downfall again. Nobody picked up Gray at the back post from a deep Mohammed Kudus corner, and he headed in unopposed, having scored his first Spurs goal against Palace in a rare win under Thomas Frank last year. De Zerbi still wanted more from his side given their numerical advantage, and he replaced Gray with Pedro Porro at the break. Van Hecke then headed in the second, and Spurs have now won three in a row for the first time in 616 days. Sage's job in doubt as Palace slip into the bottom three The result was Palace's third straight league defeat , and it leaves Sage's position in serious doubt. There was an expectation that he could be sacked if they lost this game, and the cameras caught chair Steve Parish looking less than impressed in the stand after Gray's opener. Palace did not disgrace themselves, and they have been much better in the cup competitions under Sage. However, they now sit in the bottom three, and Parish alone will decide his fate, with Sean Dyche and Frank waiting in the wings. Liverpool next for Palace before the international break Sage's next test is a home game against Liverpool before the international break, and it could be his last. Tottenham, meanwhile, have moved into the top half of the table, and De Zerbi, who used his programme notes to warn his players against complacency, will want them to keep their momentum going.

item.title: Three key reasons behind Juventus’ struggles under Luciano Spalletti
item.description: Three key reasons behind Juventus’ struggles under Luciano Spalletti Juventus are not doing very well, there’s no two ways about it. After failing to secure Champions League football last season, there were plenty of expectations from Luciano Spalletti and Co to get going this season and push higher up the table. But things don’t seem to be going well for the Bianconeri , who as things stand are just about in the top half of the Serie A table. And matters outside of their control and also favouring them. Here, we look at three main factors dictating Juve’s underwhelming start to the season. A squad in crisis Going into the summer transfer window, Spalletti needed players, and he specifically requested experienced operators across the pitch to galvanise the rest of the squad and propel his team up the ladder. However, Juve missed out on most of their targets. In goal, the likes of Alisson Becker and Emi Martínez were targeted, only for Guglielmo Vicario to arrive on loan. In midfield, Franck Kessié’s move collapsed at the eleventh hour, with Pape Matar Sarr arriving in his stead. Juve’s transfer activity left a lot to be desired, and they have since been further handicapped by an injury crisis that has particularly affected their midfield. Juve CEO Giovanni Carnevali arrived from Sassuolo just this summer. He was always going to need some time to get his feet under the table, and he could hardly have had a worse hand dealt to him. Right now, there’s no outright shining light to guide the Old Lady, and the coach seems to be going adrift as well. Tactical issues Spalletti’s football does not seem to have a clear tactical identity, and that is also affecting players on the pitch. The coach recently had to face questions regarding a tactical shift against Lecce, and while that did work at the time, that they went on to lose the following game means the clouds of doubt have persisted. Admittedly, Spalletti’s has got a lot going against him, but such is the nature of this industry that he will be the one replaced first if results don’t pick up soon. Misfiring strikers Juve’s situation in front of goal is particularly alarming. Randal Kolo Muani was brought back with a lot of effort, while Nick Woltemade arrived with a point to prove. 12 games into the season, however, they both have identically underwhelming numbers: three goals, two assists. The other option, Jeff Ekhator, is yet to feature and has been recovering from a hamstring strain. The club are already considering their options to bring in someone in January , although given both Jonathan David and Loïs Openda struggled throughout last season, the issue seems far deeper than being just about players. Juve’s attack is 13th-best in the league. 36% of their goals have come from dead-ball situations, and only two from open play. item.title: Barcelona star has already scored more goals this season than last
item.description: Barcelona star has already scored more goals this season than last A head-turning statistic surrounding the production of Barcelona star Raphinha in front of goal has come to the fore online. This comes owing to the Brazilian’s exploits in the Blaugrana’s latest outing. Hansi Flick’s troops are currently locked in action on the domestic front, in a La Liga meeting with Deportivo Alavés. The aforementioned Raphinha was for his part afforded a starting berth for the evening, as the attacking spearhead in the hosts’ frontline. And inside the opening 10 minutes, the former Leeds United man was on target for the latest occasion. Laid on just yards from goal courtesy of a perfect pull-back from Fermín López, Raphinha made no mistake in slotting home with his left foot. And in the process, Barca’s captain overtook his goalscoring tally for the entirety of the 2025/26 La Liga campaign. As per a report from statisticians Opta, after finding the net 13 times in league play last season, Raphinha has already racked up 14 goals this time round. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: UConn women’s basketball expects all injured players back for Cornell opener
item.description: STORRS — The UConn women’s basketball team appears to be getting healthy just in time for the season opener, with all three of its injured players expected to be available for Monday’s game against Cornell . Blanca Quiñonez (shoulder) and Marine Dursus (foot) sat out all three exhibition games , and Morgan Cheli (undisclosed) played in only one of them. UConn's exhibition takeaways: What we learned about UConn women’s basketball in three exhibition games UConn vs Army: UConn women's basketball vs Army | Huskies rout Knights in final exhibition game Coach Geno Auriemma said all three were back at practice, and he expects each of them to see the floor. “Fortunately, today was actually the first day that every single kid on the roster practiced,” Auriemma said after Saturday’s practice in Storrs. “So, that’s a good thing.” Quiñonez is expected to be a big piece for the Huskies this season. The sophomore forward from Ecuador is the reigning Big East Freshman and Sixth Woman of the Year after averaging 10.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.0 steals per game. #UConn coach Geno Auriemma said finding out his team’s identity will be a big part of Monday’s opener: pic.twitter.com/Da6tUSoxk2 — Nathan Canilao (@nathancanilao) October 31, 2026 Cheli, a redshirt sophomore, missed all of last season with an ankle injury. She played 24 games off the bench as a true freshman. Dursus is healing from a foot injury she has dealt with since coming over from France. She is a highly touted international player, who played for La Boulangère Wonderligue — the top women’s basketball league in France — for four seasons. “Just super excited to have Blanca, Marine and maybe Morgan,” UConn forward Sarah Strong said. “Just happy to play with them.” Auriemma noted that not all players were full participants, but he is expecting that each will be available in some capacity. “Not 100% full (participants), but they were all there, and they all did something, and some did more than others,” Auriemma said. “But again, I'm expecting everyone to be available for at least something.” Auriemma said he is not sure what to expect from the three on Monday, especially after the time Quiñonez has missed. “Let’s take Blanca, for example. No matter how many minutes she plays, it’s gonna look whatever, and you’ve got to be prepared for whatever,” Auriemma said. “You haven’t touched a basketball on the court for six months. That’s a long time to be away from the game. Same with Marine. You don’t know what you’re gonna get. Same with Morgan Cheli. You don’t know what you’re going to get. So, hopefully, whatever they can give us will be a start to what’s coming after Monday.” This article originally appeared on The Bulletin: UConn women’s basketball expects all injured players back for Cornell opener

item.title: Good News, Bad News: Tippett, Konecny Nearing Return for Flyers, But McDonald Loses His Spot
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Flyers got good news on Saturday. However, it came with a sort of bad news, or a questionable decision along with it. Starting with the good news, it looks as if Owen Tippett and Travis Konecny are nearing their return to the Flyers’ lineup, with Sunday’s 4:00 PM ET matchup with the Utah Mammoth as a possibility for both players. “I’ll talk to Konecny later today. Tippett looks like he’s trending that way, but like I said, like later this afternoon we’ll kind of know because I think they’re getting treatment and stuff like that. But they feel good,” said Flyers head coach Rick Tocchet on whether or not Tippett and Konecny will be in the lineup on Sunday. As for the signs from practice, it looks pretty clear that they’ll make their return. Both Tippett and Konecny were with the Flyers’ power play units at the beginning of practice, joining the 2nd unit alongside Oliver Bonk , Christian Dvorak , and Tyson Foerster . Alex Bump was rotating in as well, but he and Dvorak were switching. As for line rushes, both Konecny and Tippett were in their top 6 roles. Konecny was on the right wing of the Trevor Zegras-Christian Dvorak line. Tippett was on the right of Tyson Foerster and Denver Barkey . Full #Flyers lines & pairs at practice 10/31: Zegras – Dvorak – Konecny Foerster – Barkey – Tippett Martone – Cates – Martone Bump – Couturier – Bunting Sanheim – Drysdale Seeler – York Benoit – Bonk McDonald – Jiricek — Will James (@wmjsports) October 31, 2026 It sure looks like both players will be activated off of injured reserve for Sunday’s game against Utah. Jacob Gaucher was already loaned back to the Lehigh Valley Phantoms, leaving the active roster with 22 players. They needed to make one more move to create space for Konecny AND Tippett. That’s where the bad news, or questionable decision, comes in. Hunter McDonald has been loaned back to the Phantoms, which now has an active roster of 21 players, which is enough room for both forwards to return. Injecting my opinion here: I think it was the wrong move. The 24-year-old defenseman had done an excellent job with the time he was given at the NHL level. He was one of, if not the most physical players the team had during his 5-game stint. It took some adjusting, but once he was able to settle in, McDonald was playing like the best 6th defenseman the team had all season. His defensive play was solid, but his big contributions came as a physical player and an agitator. In each game, he laid a hit you were going to remember. He was not afraid of contact. Rather, he embraced it. Plus, it’s hard to forget the two instigator penalties his clean hits drew. McDonald’s hits were so big the other team came to fight him. The one against Buffalo helped put the game away. His effort against Anaheim got the Flyers a 5-on-3 early and turned into 2 goals for his team. It’s also simply poor timing. Just one game after the Flyers’ toughness and defensive efforts were questioned

item.title: Bayern Munich captain Joshua Kimmich calls Borussia Dortmund ‘unnecessary’
item.description: Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images Bayern Munich could not finish its dinner and allowed Borussia Dortmund to avoid defeat in Der Klassiker. The game finished in a 2–2 draw, with Konrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano scoring for the Bavarians—a result that Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich believes was “unnecessary.” “I think this was our third draw, and today’s result was obviously very unnecessary,” Kimmich said (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). “Especially considering how the second half unfolded, I don’t think a draw was a fair reflection of the game. But that’s football sometimes. Dortmund never gave up and kept fighting until the very end. Ultimately, we have to accept the point, even though we obviously should have won.” The result is far from ideal for Kimmich and Bayern, but they will look to pick up the pieces against Atlético Madrid in the Champions League and Mainz in the Bundesliga next weekend. item.title: Rashee Rice Returns For Chiefs As Broncos Clash Looms On Sunday
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Sunday’s matchup versus the Denver Broncos should see Rashee Rice, Kansas City Chiefs’ leading receiver, back in the starting lineup. He missed the last two weeks with a strained right hamstring but practiced fully this week. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed the team expects him to play. The return gives the Chiefs an additional offensive weapon immediately. Without Rice, the Chiefs offense struggled to find its rhythm. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes did not throw a touchdown pass in the last two games. The other receivers combined for just six catches and 39 yards in the loss to the Seahawks. Rice brings 190 yards and a touchdown from his first four games back to the mix. His presence forces defenses to respect the middle of the field. The Numbers Behind the Return Rice has 13 receptions on 16 targets through four games this season. That is a high efficiency rate that shows he is a trusted target for Mahomes. The team has missed his ability to win physical battles in coverage. Patrick Mahomes noted the specific value Rice adds to the scheme. Mahomes remarked on Wednesday that Rice is “such a physical receiver.” “He does a great job within the zone concepts at getting himself open, as well as being physical versus man [coverage].” Last week’s defeat to the Seahawks saw the Chiefs’ receiver group, featuring Xavier Worthy and rookie Cyrus Allen, tally only six catches for 39 yards. Rice’s return adds a proven target who can make plays after the catch. This gives Mahomes a safety valve in tight coverage situations. Defensive Uncertainty Remains While the offense gains a key player, the defense faces questions. Right shoulder issues caused rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to skip practice on both Thursday and Friday. Just three plays into the season-opening victory over the Broncos, he worsened that very same injury. That game saw him leave early, and he subsequently sat out the next week’s contest against the Indianapolis Colts. Delane’s injury history is concerning given his role. He sustained a hairline fracture in his scapula during the offseason, causing him to miss the Chiefs’ mandatory minicamp in June. His status for Sunday is unclear. “We’ll just see how he does here going forward,” Reid said of Delane, according to ESPN . Despite the injury, Delane showed promise when healthy. During the opener, his coverage performance against receiver Courtland Sutton was outstanding while he was on the field. This led to him intercepting quarterback Bo Nix’s intermediate pass. His absence leaves a gap in the secondary that the Broncos will try to exploit. Defensive end R Mason Thomas, another rookie, also sat out Friday’s practice due to a personal matter. However, Reid expects him to play against the Broncos. “He’ll meet us there in Denver,” Reid said of Thomas. item.title: Le Havre owners sack coach after PSG thrashing
item.description: Didier Digard has been sacked as Le Havre coach (Guillaume Saligot) Struggling French Ligue 1 club Le Havre on Saturday sacked Didier Digard as coach and accepted the resignation of chairman Jean-Michel Roussier following a 5-1 home thrashing by Paris Saint-Germain. Winless Le Havre sit bottom of Ligue 1, on just two points, and Friday's humbling defeat by PSG was the tipping point for the club's American owners Blue Crow Sports Group. In a statement, the owners said they had "accepted the principle of Mr. Jean-Michel Roussier's resignation from his position as chairman". That resignation will be formalised at a board of directors meeting on Thursday. "Furthermore, Le Havre Athletic Club has notified its coach, Didier Digard, of his precautionary suspension pending further decisions within the framework of ongoing proceedings," they added. The club has appointed Jair Karam, the youth teams director, as interim coach to take charge of the first team from Monday for the resumption of training. Digard is the second coach sacked so far this season after Lens fired German coach Dino Toppmoeller after just six league games in charge. ah-cto/lp/dmc/pb

item.title: Konrad Laimer reflects on the impact of Bayern Munich’s injuries in draw with Borussia Dortmund
item.description: Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images | Getty Images Konrad Laimer and Dayot Upamecano scored for Bayern Munich, who couldn’t keep a clean sheet nor secure the win as Borussia Dortmund elbowed their way to a 2-2 draw. item.title: Roma’s Bryan Cristante not taking Manchester United for granted ahead of CL clash
item.description: Roma’s Bryan Cristante not taking Manchester United for granted ahead of CL clash Serie A giants Roma picked up a dominant 5-2 win over Udinese and continued their march upwards in the project under Gian Piero Gasperini. They now find themselves at third in the table, only behind Inter and Lazio but face a big challenge in the form of Manchester United in the Champions League in midweek. Bryan Cristante, who scored in the first half against Udinese, spoke about the upcoming tie and he made it clear that despite their struggles, Manchester United can’t be taken for granted at all. The Italian told DAZN – via VoceGiallorossa : “Yes, but it’s still Manchester United. They’re a strong team with a lot of quality players. It will be very difficult to play at their home ground, because they’ll want to do well and certainly bounce back.” “But we’ll go there and try to bring it home, as we always do. We’re taking it game by game, and clearly getting a positive result would be crucial for our Champions League position.” He also looked at Roma’s performance against Udinese, appearing proud that the Giallorossi score a lot of goals regularly. “Yes, definitely. We’re scoring a lot and creating a lot, and that’s very important. It’s clear that if you score, it’s easier to win. So, the longer we can keep this up, the better.” Cristante was also asked about whether Roma can keep up their performances until the end of the season. He responded: “We’re trying, of course. It’s difficult; there are so many games and so many strong teams. But if we play like this, we have a chance. We have to compete to stay there as long as possible. It’s not easy; there’s so much at stake, but as long as we’re there, we’ll do everything we can to be there.” Roma have won once in three Champions League games. They did impress a lot against Real Madrid but fell prey to an impressive, late comeback from Los Blancos. Manchester United have won just twice in all competitions and lie in complete contrast to the Giallorossi, who will come as a positive for Gasperini. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

Larison, 24, will serve as the third option in the running back room behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner after an illness thinned the depth chart. The 5-foot-11, 209-pound change of pace reverted to the practice squad in September after making his NFL debut versus the Seattle Seahawks. item.title: Undefeated Bethlehem earns Section 2 Class AA boys' soccer championship
item.description: Bethlehem celebrates after beating Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake for the Section 2, Class AA title on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at LaSalle Institute in Troy, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) TROY - Not a single opponent has been able to find the blueprint to defeating the Bethlehem boys' soccer team this season. That continued through Saturday's Section 2 Class AA championship between Bethlehem and Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, as the top-seeded Eagles remained unbeaten on the season and captured their second sectional title in three seasons by gutting out a 1-0 win over the No. 2 Spartans at La Salle Institute. "We've got a huge senior group, so, obviously, it's the last time for them. Doing this with them is a big deal," Bethlehem coach Brian Spina said. "It's my fourth year now as the head coach. I watch our younger teams constantly and, as they're coming up, you always hope for a team like this." "This is just an insane feeling," Bethlehem senior forward Ayaz Sajid said. "I've been playing with these guys forever and we all love each other. We all had the same goal in the beginning of the season and we were able to accomplish that." The game remained scoreless until Bethlehem senior midfielder Orson Wagg found the back of the net with 28:25 remaining. Senior defender Ian NeJame provided the assist. "I made sure to get a head on that one," Wagg said. "When I saw it in the air, I made sure to attack it and not just let it come to me. I think that taking that stance and just gambling … paid off - and, then, we scored." Key moment The Spartans appeared to draw even at 1-1 with 4:48 left to play, but their would-be goal was wiped out by an offside call. Bethlehem did not allow a goal in any of its Section 2 playoff games. Star of the game Wagg provided all the offense his team needed as he scored Bethlehem's first goal since October 22 in the Eagles' quarterfinal win over Amsterdam. Bethlehem had advanced to Saturday's final on penalty kicks against Niskayuna on Monday following a scoreless draw. "I'm happy for him, happy for the group," Spina said. "We worked hard. We talk a lot about patience and building into the next opportunity, so we had a couple in the first half we liked, but didn't quite execute. For him to go and finish like that in the second half was huge for us." Numbers to know 13: Shutouts the Bethlehem defense, paced by junior goalie Parker Mooney, has posted this season. 8: Consecutive wins Burnt Hills had earned entering Saturday. 5: Yellow cards that the teams combined to draw. What's next Bethlehem: The Eagles (16-0-2), ranked second in the state Class AA poll, will take on Section 3 champion Watertown (18-0), ranked No. 1 in the state, at 2 p.m. next Saturday at Waterford-Halfmoon High School. Burnt Hills: The Spartans, who were denied in their quest for their first sectional title since 2019 (Class A), wrapped up their season with an 11-5-2 showing. item.title: Match Recap: Bayern Munich’s painful 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund
item.description: (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund played out a wild 2-2 Klassiker at the Allianz Arena on Saturday, but the result was about as frustrating as it gets for the Rekordmeister . Bayern Munich had the chances, controlled the game, and twice took the lead. Somehow, it still co uldn’t finish the job. The scoring started in the 38th minute when Konrad Laimer pounced on a rebound after Michael Olise set him up for a dangerous opportunity. That came shortly after referee Tobias S tieler, following a VAR review, controversially disallowed a Jobe Bellingham goal for Borussia Dortmund because Carney Chukwuemeka interfered with goalk eeper Jonas Urbig while in an offside position. FC Bayern had an opportunity to double its advantage in the 56th minute when a Felix Nmecha handball resulted in a penalty. Unfortunately, Harry Kane sent his effort crashing against the crossbar. Dortmund immediately capitalized, wit h Serhou Guirassy equalizing in the 60th minute. Dayot Upamecano restored Bayern’s lead six mi nutes later, converting a Kane assist following a Joshua Kimmich corner. Kane later hit the post, and Lennart Karl rattle d the crossbar in stoppage time. Dortmund, however, had the final say, with substitute Fábio Silva scoring in the 89th minut e to steal a point. As if dropping two points wasn’t enough, Bayern also suffered three injury setbacks. Ismaël Saib ari (ankle) and Serge Gnabry (thigh) both left in the first half, while Olise was forced off in the 84th minute. The final statistics showed Bayern with 56% possessi on, 23 shots, and 4.18 xG compared to Dortmund’s 0.63. Six b ig chances created, four missed, and two points dropped. Bayern Munich remains atop the Bundesliga on goal differential, but the injury situation is becoming a serious concern with Atlético Madrid looming in the Champions League. A frustrating afternoon, an exhausting Klassiker , and potentially three significant injury headaches. Bayern Munich probably deserved better than this, but the game…is the game. item.title: Ole Miss uses explosive second half to blow out Auburn, 45-15
item.description: OXFORD, MS - OCTOBER 31: Ole Miss Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) passes the ball during the game between the Auburn Tigers and the Ole Miss Rebels on October 31, 2026 at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS.(Photo by Jason Homan/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 12 Ole Miss Rebels overcame a slow start in the first half and poured in 31 second half points en route to a 45-15 victory over Auburn in Oxford. Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) scored 21 points in the fourth quarter, and its defense held the Tigers to only 63 rushing yards. The absence of an injured Kewan Lacy didn’t have the impact some commentators thought with Ole Miss gaining 224 yards rushing. Trinidad Chambliss didn’t have a perfect game, but his 22/34 passing for 263 yards, two touchdowns and one interception along with 65 rushing yards and another touchdown was plenty good enough. Things even got comfortable enough to allow back-up QB Deuce Knight to score the final touchdown of the game against his former team on a 17 yard scramble to the end zone. The first half was an ugly one with Ole Miss going into the locker room with a 14-9 lead. Auburn had an extra point blocked, and the teams traded turnovers in a sluggish first and second quarter that was giving some weird Halloween maybe even Auburn Jesus vibes. But the second half was a completely different game though Auburn closed the lead to 17-15 with a third quarter touchdown run by QB Byrum Brown. Chambliss answered with a 26 yard touchdown run to make it 24-15, and Ole Miss never looked back from there. While Auburn started 4/5 on third down conversions, it finished at 7/14, which is still a far cry from where fans would like it to be. The defense played much better and confidence grew as the offense expanded its lead again and again. Caleb Cunningham and Horatio Fields each had a receiving touchdown with Fields being the leader in receiving yards for the day with 73 yards on six catches. The Ole Miss defense registered four sacks with two each from Tah’j Butler and Suntarine Perkins. Now Ole Miss can enjoy the win for the rest of its Saturday, but when fans and the team wake up on Sunday, all attention will shift to an enormous game against the Georgia Bulldogs set for a prime time kickoff in Oxford. The Rebels will be looking to defend its 16-game home winning streak.

item.description: For Pope Leo XIV, choosing sides between two Catholic universities might ordinarily be considered a breach of papal diplomacy. But when Villanova and Notre Dame tip off the college basketball season in Rome on Sunday, the man beneath the white robes faces a temptation of an entirely different sort: rooting for his alma mater. Fortunately, the first American-born pope devised a loophole: Pope Leo XIV will remain above the fray, his allegiance safely concealed beneath the papal robes. Robert Prevost, the Villanova graduate who happens to wear those robes, is free to harbor considerably less impartial sentiments. “Growing up on the South Side of Chicago, we oftentimes heard, ‘Go Irish!'” Leo XIV told a crowd of roughly 7,000 players, coaches and supporters from Villanova and Notre Dame at the Vatican on Saturday, drawing applause. “But, as you all know, Prevost graduated from Villanova,” he continued, prompting even louder cheers. “So the pope doesn’t take sides. The event, organized to celebrate the election of the first American pope, will open the 2026-27 college basketball season. Leo XIV, born Robert Francis Prevost in Chicago, graduated from Villanova in 1977 with a mathematics degree, decades before his papal election in May 2025. item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Los Angeles Angels don’t often deal with each other, especially under soon-to-be-former owner Arte Moreno , but a “wild” trade proposal from Bleacher Report’s Zachary D. Rymer has them doing just that. Rymer’s trade proposal has the Dodgers sending three young stars in Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Justin Wrobleski to Orange County in exchange for shortstop Zach Neto, who the Angels nearly dealt at the trade deadline. “According to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe , the ask of the Boston Red Sox in August was for no less than Franklin Arias, MLB’s No. 2 prospect,” Rymer wrote. “…For the Dodgers, the equivalent of an Arias-led package would be something involving No. 4-ranked prospect Josue De Paula. But what if they overwhelmed the Angels with controllable major leaguers instead? Wrobleski has already been an All-Star, while Rushing and Sasaki have teased that kind of upside. All three are in their 20s and controlled through at least 2030.” May 15, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing (68) shakes hands with relief pitcher Justin Wrobleski (70) in ninth inning of a 12-2 defeat of the Athletics at Dodger Stadium . Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why Doesn’t This Trade Work? This trade wouldn’t work for the Dodgers for a number of reasons, but let’s start with the obvious: The Dodgers have a shortstop. Mookie Betts has held down the left side of the middle infield for the Dodgers for two seasons now, accruing 8.8 bWAR over those two seasons. Granted, that’s lower than the 25-year-old Neto’s 10.5 bWAR, moving Betts elsewhere would disrupt the Dodgers’ positional depth. Additionally, sending those three players to the Angels would be a massive overpay by the Dodgers given their roles in the team. Wrobleski and Sasaki are primed for bigger roles in 2027 should the Dodgers choose not to add another starting pitcher, and both had great seasons in their own rights. Prior to the All-Star Game, Wrobleski had a 2.69 ERA through 16 appearances for the Dodgers, and earned his spot to represent the National League at the Midsummer Classic . Sasaki took over the latter half of the season, posting a 2.83 ERA through 10 appearances. Rushing is also a key players for the Dodgers, and had a great year despite his injury troubles. He hit 12 homers and drove in 36 RBIs, both personal bests, and had an .812 OPS heading into the All-Star break. Is Zach Neto Worth That Much? On the other side of the trade, Neto hit 27 homers and drove in 77 RBIs on the year with a .766 OPS. Dominating the expected goals (xG) battle with a staggering 4.18 to Dortmund's 0.63, the hosts failed to translate their tactical superiority into a victory.
